brief.subject: Election night tax votes, record IRS haul, Trump account rules
brief.headline: State Tax Ballot Results, Record IRS Collections and Trump Account Rule Hearing
brief.dek: Washington keeps its high-earner tax, California's billionaire tax lags, Colorado is undecided, and the IRS reports a $5.6 trillion year.
brief.lede: Tuesday's ballot measures are reshaping state taxes on high earners and homeowners. Owners in Washington, California, Colorado and Florida should watch final counts closely.

sections.heading: State Tax Measures: Early Results
bullets: Washington: voters are keeping the new high-earners income tax and rejecting a repeal, which matters for profitable owners there.
California: a proposed wealth tax on billionaires was behind in early returns after heavy opposition spending.
Colorado: a plan to replace the flat income tax with tiered rates is too close to call.
Florida: Amendment 3 passed, sharply cutting property taxes on owner-occupied homes and bringing state budget cuts.

sections.heading: IRS Posts Record Collections
bullets: $5.6 trillion: total taxes the IRS collected in the fiscal year, per its Oct. 29 report.
That haul rose nearly 5% from 2025, a record for the agency.
Refunds also grew larger in 2026, a useful benchmark when setting client expectations.

sections.heading: Trump Account Investment Rules
bullets: The IRS has scheduled a hearing on proposed rules defining eligible investments for Trump accounts.
The proposal was first published in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026.
Until the year the beneficiary turns 18, the account may hold only these eligible investments.

items.title: The Bookkeeping Mistake That Keeps Showing Up in New Clients’ Books
items.snippet: The fix itself is unglamorous, which is exactly why it works and why it is worth explaining to clients in plain terms rather than as a process document.

items.title: IRS Reports Record Tax Collections, Larger Refunds in 2026
items.snippet: According to an Oct. 29 report from the agency, the IRS collected $5.6 trillion in taxes during the fiscal year, an increase of nearly 5% from 2025.

items.title: California Billionaire Tax Trailing in Early Returns
items.snippet: A proposed first-in-the-nation wealth tax on California’s billionaires trailed in early returns Tuesday after a contentious campaign that saw heavy spending by wealthy opponents.

items.title: Washington Voters Upholding ‘Millionaires Tax’ in Tuesday Vote
items.snippet: In Washington's biggest tax fight in decades, voters were backing the state's new high-earners income tax in Tuesday's vote count, rejecting an initiative that would repeal it.

items.title: Colorado’s Tiered Income Tax Proposal Now Too Close to Call
items.snippet: Colorado voters are split on the proposal to eliminate the state’s flat rate in favor of a tiered income tax system, under which higher-income earners face a bigger tax liability.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Guidance on Eligible Investments for Trump Accounts; Hearing
items.snippet: This document provides a notice of proposed rulemaking (CC- 00349938-26) published in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026. The proposed regulations provided guidance regarding eligible investments, which are the only assets in which the Trump account may be invested before the first day of the calendar year in which the account beneficiary attains 18.

items.title: Florida’s Amendment 3 Passes, Bringing Property Tax Change and Budget Cuts
items.snippet: In a year where cost of living is front of mind for voters, Floridians approved a constitutional amendment that would significantly cut property taxes for people who own the homes they live in.

items.title: Canopy Reveals General Availability of AI Tax Workflow Automation
items.snippet: Canopy announced Tuesday the general availability of Tax Workflow Automation, described as an AI-powered suite that takes tax work from the first document request to the signed, paid return in one connected workflow.
